extracted.intended_audience: public company registrants and their advisors (including Accelerated Filers (AFs), Large Accelerated Filers (LAFs), Smaller Reporting Companies (SRCs), Emerging Growth Companies (EGCs), and foreign private issuers)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts the SEC final rule requirements and evaluative standards for disclosing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions (Scopes 1 and 2), related methodological and boundary disclosures, timing and filing mechanics, limited exemptions, and attestation requirements for certain filers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard unit: aggregate CO2e
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule will require the disclosure of any described scope of emissions to be expressed in the aggregate in terms of CO2e.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change is intended to address commenter concerns about additional burdens without material investor benefit and to provide a standard unit familiar to many registrants to simplify disclosure and enhance comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disaggregate individually material constituent gases
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registrant is required to disclose its Scope 1 and/or Scope 2 emissions, and any constituent gas of the disclosed emissions is individually material, it must also disclose such constituent gas disaggregated from the other gases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if methane is included in a GHG reduction target and is reasonably likely to materially affect the registrant's business, it may be material and therefore required to be disclosed separately. Disaggregated disclosure helps investors assess exposure to transition risk as markets and governments may treat components differently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gross terms excluding offsets
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant that is required to disclose its Scope 1 and/or Scope 2 emissions must disclose those emissions in gross terms by excluding the impact of any purchased or generated offsets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This enables investors to understand the full magnitude of transition risk exposure and to assess reliance on offsets, particularly if the registrant provides separate disclosure about offsets pursuant to Item 1504.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe methodology, significant inputs, and significant assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrant must describe the methodology, significant inputs, and significant assumptions used to calculate the registrant's disclosed GHG emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule allows registrants flexibility to present this information in a manner that fits their facts and circumstances while requiring sufficient contextual information for investors to understand scope and comparability across registrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose organizational boundaries and method used
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant must disclose the organizational boundaries used when calculating its Scope 1 emissions and/or its Scope 2 emissions, and disclose the method used to determine those boundaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If organizational boundaries materially differ from the scope of entities and operations included in the registrant's consolidated financial statements, the registrant must provide a brief explanation of the difference in sufficient detail for a reasonable investor to understand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility to use control approaches (e.g., GHG Protocol methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrant may use one of the methods for determining control under the GHG Protocol, including the operational control approach, as long as it discloses the method used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach provides flexibility to choose an appropriate control method while requiring disclosure of the method so investors can understand the scope of entities and operations included in the GHG calculation relative to financial statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief discussion of operational boundaries and categorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrant must provide a brief discussion, in sufficient detail for a reasonable investor to understand, of the operational boundaries used, including the approach to categorization of emissions and emissions sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to give investors a general understanding of which sources were included for Scope 1 (direct) and Scope 2 (indirect) calculations and to enhance comparability while avoiding overly burdensome disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief description of protocol/standard, calculation approach, emission factor types/sources, and tools
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule requires a brief description of the protocol or standard used to report the GHG emissions, including the calculation approach, the type and source of any emission factors used, and any calculation tools used to calculate the GHG emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrant should disclose whether it used the GHG Protocol's Corporate Accounting and Reporting Standard, an EPA regulation, an applicable ISO standard, or another standard, and identify any calculation tools (e.g., GHG Protocol or ISO tools). The Commission clarified it will not require disclosure of quantitative emission factors, only the type and source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope 2 method disclosure (location-based vs market-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrant should disclose whether it calculated its Scope 2 emissions using a particular method (such as the location-based method, market-based method, or both).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope 2 may use a method that differs from Scope 1; disclosure of the method supports investor understanding and comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify calculation tools used
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrant should disclose the identity of any calculation tools used to calculate GHG emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include tools provided by the GHG Protocol or pursuant to ISO standards; naming tools helps investors evaluate the approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose type and source of emission factors (not quantitative values)
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rule requires disclosure of the type and source of any emission factors used but does not require disclosure of quantitative emission factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: disclose use of EPA emission factors for stationary combustion/mobile combustion of fuel types. This provides context for investors without demanding detailed factor-level disclosure that may be immaterial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted use of reasonable estimates with explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant may use reasonable estimates when disclosing its GHG emissions provided it also describes the assumptions underlying, and its reasons for using, the estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes that direct measurement at source may not be possible; requiring descriptions of assumptions/reasons helps investors assess reliability and comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope 3 disclosure voluntary (not required)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission is not adopting a provision to require registrants to disclose Scope 3 emissions at this time; disclosure of Scope 3 remains voluntary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale includes potential burdens, data reliability concerns, and evolving methodologies. Registrants may still disclose Scope 3 (including upstream/downstream) and international/state requirements may influence voluntary disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption for SRCs and EGCs from GHG emissions requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule will exempt Smaller Reporting Companies (SRCs) and Emerging Growth Companies (EGCs) from any requirement to disclose their GHG emissions, including Scopes 1 and 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent with a scaled disclosure approach to limit burdens on these smaller issuers while requiring them to comply with other climate-related disclosure requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion for manure management systems
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant is not required to include GHG emissions from a manure management system when disclosing its overall Scopes 1 and 2 emissions pursuant to 17 CFR 229.1505(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This exclusion is based on the 2023 Consolidated Appropriations Act restriction on using funds to implement mandatory reporting of GHG emissions from manure management systems; applies so long as federal law restricts implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure timing: most recently completed fiscal year and previously disclosed historical years
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registrant is required to disclose its Scope 1 and/or Scope 2 emissions, it must disclose those emissions for its most recently completed fiscal year and, to the extent previously disclosed in a Commission filing, for the historical fiscal year(s) included in the consolidated financial statements included in the filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A registrant that has not previously disclosed Scopes 1 and 2 emissions in a Commission filing for a historical fiscal year is not required to estimate and report those emissions for such period; this limits historical-period compliance burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference timing accommodation for Form 10-K filers
rubrics_metrics.description: GHG emissions metrics required in an annual report on Form 10-K may be incorporated by reference from the registrant's Form 10-Q for the second fiscal quarter in the fiscal year immediately following the year to which the GHG emissions metrics disclosure relates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledges practical difficulty of measuring/reporting by the 10-K deadline; accommodates market practice where many registrants report such metrics after completion of the second fiscal quarter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign private issuer timing and filing mechanics (Form 20-F)
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign private issuers may disclose GHG emissions metrics required by Item 1505 in an amendment to their annual report on Form 20-F due no later than 225 days after the fiscal year end to which the disclosure relates; the disclosure must be provided in an amendment (not a Form 6-K) to be treated as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This corresponds approximately to the domestic second-quarter Form 10-Q filing deadline and requires an express statement in the annual report indicating intention to incorporate by reference or amend the filing to give notice to investors where to find the information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration statement timing (Securities Act/Exchange Act registration statements)
rubrics_metrics.description: GHG emissions metrics for a Securities Act or Exchange Act registration statement must be provided as of the most recently completed fiscal year that is at least 225 days prior to the registration statement's date of effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a calendar year-end LAF filing an S-1 that goes effective on or after Aug 7 must use 2027 metrics (225+ days after 2027 fiscal year-end); if effective earlier than 225 days, the registrant may use the prior fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation requirement for AFs and LAFs (scope and report contents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed rules would require a registrant that is an AF or an LAF to include in the relevant filing an attestation report covering the disclosure of its Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions and to provide certain related disclosures about the service provider providing the attestation report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed rules include requirements related to the service provider, the engagement, and the attestation report. The Commission explained attestation provides additional reliability regarding figures, assumptions, methodologies, and data sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phased assurance levels (limited to reasonable assurance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed attestation engagement would be performed at a 'limited assurance' level for fiscal years 2 and 3 after the Scopes 1 and 2 emissions disclosure compliance date and at a 'reasonable assurance' level for fiscal year 4 and beyond (with AFs and LAFs permitted to obtain reasonable assurance earlier at their option).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phased approach intended to mitigate cost/burden, allow time for registrants to develop DCPs and for assurance providers to prepare. Voluntary assurance by other registrants would be permitted but subject to certain disclosure requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum qualifications, independence, and attestation report requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed minimum standards include: minimum qualifications and independence requirements for the attestation service provider and minimum requirements for the accompanying attestation report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission stated these minimum standards aim to improve accuracy, comparability, and reliability of GHG emissions reporting while providing some flexibility given evolving assurance practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: No specific attestation standard mandated
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission did not propose to create or adopt a specific attestation standard for assuring GHG emissions, recognizing that reporting and attestation landscapes are evolving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The approach provides flexibility so as not to curtail future innovations in reporting and attestation; the Commission acknowledged this will not eliminate fragmentation but believed flexibility was warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assurance not required for Scope 3
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission did not propose requiring assurance of Scope 3 emissions disclosure because preparing such disclosure presents unique challenges (e.g., obtaining activity data from suppliers/customers, verification difficulties).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope 3 assurance was excluded due to burdens, potential costs, and data gaps relative to Scopes 1 and 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: GHG intensity disclosure not required
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike the proposal, the final rule will not require registrants to disclose GHG emissions in terms of intensity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters noted investors can calculate emissions per unit of revenue themselves by dividing gross GHG emissions by total revenues; eliminating intensity reduces compliance burden though registrants may voluntarily disclose intensity.
